title: Hot cocoa bombs
subtitle: chocolate spheres that melt into hot chocolate
excerpt: Hot cocoa bombs are hollow chocolate spheres filled with cocoa powder, sugar, and mini marshmallows. You lower one into a mug, pour over hot milk, and watch the sphere melt and release its contents. The technique requires silicone hemisphere moulds and a little patience joining the halves, but the result is actually theatrical, and the hot chocolate itself is richer than a standard stirred-in mix.
sourceNotes: Hot cocoa bombs became a viral social media phenomenon in late 2020, though the concept of a hollow chocolate shell melted by hot liquid is older, appearing in restaurant plated desserts from at least the early 2000s. The home version using silicone hemisphere moulds became widely replicated through the winter of 2020,2021. The technique is derived from chocolate moulding and shell-making used in professional confectionery; the novelty here is using it for a hot drink format.

recipe.batchNotes: Keep at cool room temperature in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 weeks ahead; store in a cool spot.

content.text: Hot cocoa bombs are hollow chocolate spheres filled with cocoa and marshmallows that melt dramatically when hot milk is poured over them. They need silicone hemisphere moulds (available cheaply online) and two coats of chocolate for a shell thick enough not to crack when you handle it. The finished bombs keep for two weeks and make excellent gifts.

Melt the milk chocolate in a heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water. Stir until smooth, then remove from the heat. Spoon about 1½ tablespoons of melted chocolate into each hemisphere mould cavity. Rotate and tilt the mould so the chocolate coats the inside completely, going right up to the rim. Place the mould in the freezer for 5 minutes until set. Apply a second coat in the same way, pushing the chocolate up the edges where it is thinnest. Freeze for a further 15 minutes.

Carefully flex the silicone mould to release 12 chocolate hemispheres. Mix the cocoa powder and caster sugar together. Half-fill 6 hemispheres with the cocoa mix and a small handful of mini marshmallows. Heat a flat plate in the microwave for 30 seconds until warm. Press an empty hemisphere rim-down onto the warm plate for a few seconds to melt the edge slightly, then press it firmly onto a filled half. Hold for 20 seconds until the join sets. Repeat for all 6 bombs. Refrigerate for 15 minutes to firm the seam.

Drizzle the finished bombs with a little extra melted chocolate and dust lightly with cocoa powder if you like. To serve, place a bomb in a large mug and pour 250 ml of hot (not boiling) whole milk slowly over it. The sphere will crack open and the cocoa and marshmallows will disperse. Stir briefly and drink.
